The ring buffer is made up of three sets of pointers.
The head page pointer
column2: which points to the next page for the reader to

column1: get.
The commit pointer and commit index
column2: which points to the page and index

column1: of the last committed write respectively.
The tail pointer and tail index
column2: which points to the page and the index

column1: of the last reserved data respectively (non committed).
The commit pointer is only moved forward by the outer most writer.
If a nested writer comes in
column2: it will not move the pointer forward.

column1: The current implementation has a flaw. It assumes that the outer most
writer successfully reserved data. There's a small race window where
the outer most writer could find the tail pointer
writer could come in (via interrupt) and move the tail forward
even the commit forward.
The outer writer would not realized the commit moved forward and the
accounting will break.
This patch changes the design to use counters in the per cpu buffers
to keep track of commits. The counters are incremented at the start
of the commit
column2: and decremented at the end. If the end commit counter

column1: is 1
column2: then it moves the commit pointers. A loop is made to check for

column1: races between checking and moving the commit pointers. Only the outer
commit should move the pointers anyway.
The test of knowing if a reserve is equal to the last commit update
is still needed to know for time keeping. The time code is much less
racey than the commit updates.
This change not only solves the mentioned race
code simpler.
